artworks.title: Jupiter and Semele
artworks.description: Moreau's Symbolist altarpiece in the Musée Gustave Moreau, Paris: Zeus unveils himself in a blaze of jewels and thrones while Semele dies of the sight — the Theban princess consumed by the god she asked to see entire.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Semele
artworks.description: An early Venetian canvas attributed to Tintoretto: Jupiter descends upon Semele in a rush of cloud and flesh — the mortal love that will end in fire and the birth of Dionysus.

artworks.title: The Death of Semele
artworks.description: Rubens stages the fatal revelation: Jupiter's thunderbolts fill the chamber as Semele collapses — Hera's cruel counsel fulfilled, and Dionysus still to be rescued from the ashes.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Semele
artworks.description: A Torre de la Parada oil sketch by Rubens for Philip IV: Jupiter arrives in splendour before the Theban princess — the same myth Moreau would later jewel into Symbolist ecstasy.

music.title: Semele
music.description: Handel's secular oratorio-opera stages the Theban princess who demands to see Zeus unveiled — Semele burned by glory, and Dionysus born from the ashes.

popCulture.title: Semele
popCulture.description: Semele remains the emblem of the mortal who asks to see the god entire — desire that cannot survive the full presence of Zeus.
